newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesia's tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were generally stable in late trading on Tuesday amid sluggish buying interest, traders said.
Traders said a deal was done in the afternoon at 47.25 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for August shipment, slightly lower than the overnight deal at 47.75.
"There has been some sporadic buying today, but demand itself is not high. It's safe to say the market is generally stable," said one trader.
Traders said offer prices were unchanged at 48.00 fob Medan, at 47.75-48.00 fob Surabaya, at 47.50 fob Padang and at 46.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
They said supply was a little bit tight in Medan because many tappers had shifted to other jobs when rubber prices were still considered low for them.
"There are always other things to do for the tappers and when the business is slow. They can become workers in construction work, for instance," said another trader.
He said supply was also tight in Palembang in South Sumatra, but mainly because of the continuing rain in the province.
